title: Hubble: Decagon Around Saturn's South Pole
explanation:
# Saturn's Mysterious Geometric Poles

Saturn's north and south poles are crowned with strikingly different geometric cloud patterns—a stable hexagon (six-sided shape) that has persisted for over 40 years at the north pole, and a newly observed decagon (ten-sided shape) swirling around the south pole—formed when fast-moving winds colliding with slower polar air create wave patterns that somehow organize themselves into these precise, multi-sided shapes. Scientists are still puzzled by why these geometric boundaries form and persist on Saturn, making these alien wind systems one of the solar system's most intriguing mysteries.
